title: ZDX administration API: department and location lookups

prose.text: Despite its name, the ZDX administration API is a lookup of departments and locations used to filter other reads. The help lists it that way, [[shared.log-export.zdx:api-scope]].

prose.label: In the SDKs.
prose.text: {{python-departments-docstring}} {{sdk-records-id-name}} The SDKs do not send the same search parameter {{divergence:search-param}}. The Python hours shorthand applies to these lookups too, [[zdx.sdk-python.request-shaping:since-to-epoch]].

prose.label: Open.
prose.text: What the time range means for a list of departments or locations is not stated {{gap:time-filter-semantics}}, and how the search parameters match is open {{gap:q-vs-search}}.

checks.do: Whether a department or location filter uses an ID the lookup returned, rather than a name.
Whether a name search sends `q`, the parameter the contract defines, when results look unfiltered.

departments-op.statement: The departments lookup gets the configured departments.

locations-op.statement: The locations lookup gets Zscaler locations, returning all configured locations when no search filter is given.

expect.description: Gets Zscaler locations. All configured Zscaler locations are returned if the search filters is not specified.

q-param.statement: In the contract both lookups take optional query parameters `from` and `to` (int64 integers) and `q`.

ids-as-filters.statement: The department and location IDs these lookups return are the values the report reads take as `dept` and `loc` filters.
ids-as-filters.conditions: Inferred from matching names and integer ID types: the lookups return objects with integer `id`, and the report operations (for example the application list) take `dept` and `loc` as integer arrays. The contract does not state the link.

administration-reads-only.statement: The contract's Administration operations are all reads of departments and locations (and of a department's users); none creates, changes or manages administrator accounts.
administration-reads-only.conditions: Rests on the eight operations tagged Administration in the captured contract at the pin, all GET: the two lookups above and /v1/config/departments, its summary, a department by ID, a department's users, /v1/config/locations and a location by ID.

config-lookups.statement: The configuration area has its own directory reads: departments and locations filtered by a search query (other filters are ignored when an `id` is given), a summarized department list of only ID and name, and location groups.

expect.description: Gets a list of departments. Can be filtered by a search query. If `id` is provided, other filters are ignored.
Gets a list of locations. Can be filtered by a search query. If `id` is provided, other filters are ignored.
Gets a summarized list of departments, returning only ID and name. Can be filtered by various parameters.
Gets a list of location groups. Can be filtered by a search query. If `id` is provided, other filters are ignored.

python-departments-docstring.statement: The Python `list_departments` docstring says it 'Returns the list of Admin Users enrolled in the Client Connector Portal', although the method reads `/administration/departments` and the same docstring says it returns configured departments.

evidence.after: def list_departments(self, query_params: Optional[dict] = None) -> APIResult[List[Administration]]:
quotes: Returns the list of Admin Users enrolled in the Client Connector Portal.

sdk-records-id-name.statement: Both SDKs read each department and location as an ID and a name: the Python lookups build the `Administration` model (`id`, `name`) and the Go `Department` and `Location` structs hold `ID` and `Name`, while the contract's department record also carries `comments`, `deleted`, `idpId`, `isForUnauthenticatedUser` and `isNonEditable`. The Python `Departments` and `Locations` models in `common.py`, which also read `num_devices`, are used by the alert models, not by these lookups.

comments.description: Additional information or comments about this department.

idpId.description: The unique identifier for the IdP associated with this department.

isForUnauthenticatedUser.description: Indicates if this is an internally-created department for unauthenticated users. This is a read-only field.

isNonEditable.description: Indicates if the department is not editable by the current user. This is a read-only field.

time-filter-semantics.title: What a time range means on the department and location lookups
time-filter-semantics.detail: Both lookups accept `from` and `to`. Whether the range selects departments and locations with active devices in that window, or has another meaning for reference data, is not documented; the help describes the area as listing the active locations and departments.
time-filter-semantics.blocks: complete department and location lists for filters

q-vs-search.title: How the lookups' search parameters match, and whether `search` is honored
q-vs-search.detail: The contract defines `q` on both lookups. The Go SDK sends `search` on both and also `q` on locations; the Python SDK documents `search`. Whether the server honors `search`, and whether `q` matches exactly or partially and by name or ID, is not documented.
q-vs-search.blocks: filtering departments and locations by name

search-param.summary: The lookups' search parameter: the contract defines `q`; the Go departments filter sends `search` (the locations filter has both `search` and `q`); the Python decorator sends a `search` argument as `q`.

positions.says: The Go departments filter sends `search` and has no `q`.

search-param.impact: If the server honors only `q`, a Go department search returns every department rather than the match, while the same search through Python is filtered.
